title: Three-colour triangle Ramsey number is at most 17
statement: Let $r_3 = r(3,3,3)$ denote the three-colour Ramsey number for triangles, that is, the least $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ with three colours contains a monochromatic triangle. Then $r_3 \le 17$; equivalently, every $3$-edge-colouring of $K_{17}$ admits three vertices whose three connecting edges all receive the same colour.
